newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai coffee policy meet delayed pending new govt.
newsitem.headline: Thai coffee policy meet delayed pending new govt.

text.p: A Thai government meeting on 1996/97 (October-September) coffee policy has been postponed to next month pending the appointment of the new government, a senior commerce ministry official told Reuters on Friday.
The meeting, originally scheduled for November 30, will bring the government and the coffee industry together to discuss coffee prices and export policy.
"I'm quite positive that the meeting could take place soon after the cabinet is sworn in... perhaps by December 15," said Manas Soiploy, a director of the ministry's agricultural trade division.
The government of Prime Minister-designate Chavalit Yongchaiyudh is expected to be sworn in on December 1.
Narongchai Akrasanee, a finance executive know for his strong support for free trade, is tipped to be the next commerce minister.
There had been rumours earlier that the government might seek to guarantee local planters a coffee price of 30 baht ($1.20) per kg.
Thailand exported about 60,000 tonnes of coffee beans in 1995 from an estimated total output of 78,801 tonnes, according to official figures.
The agriculture ministry has forecast coffee output this year at 81,398 tonnes.
